newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore's Lee said discharged from hospital.
newsitem.headline: Singapore's Lee said discharged from hospital.

text.p: Singapore Senior Minister Lee Kwan Yew was discharged from hospital on Sunday, a spokeswoman for Singapore General Hospital said on Monday.
"It was a successful stay," she told Reuters.
She declined to give details of the results of the tests on the former prime minister's bladder.
Officials at Lee's office were not immediately available for comment.
The city-state's long-time former prime minister entered hospital on Saturday for scheduled tests.
The office of Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong issued a brief statement on Saturday saying Lee, 73, had had chronic inflammatory tissue removed from the wall of his bladder on two previous occasions.
"His stay in hospital will depend upon the extent of the operation," it said. It gave no other details of his condition.
Lee, who led Singapore for 31 years until 1990 and remains in the cabinet, retains considerable political influence.
He had two heart operations in early 1996, raising fears of a drop on local financial markets.
The markets took the news in their stride, however, a reaction which Lee said afterwards proved Singapore had accepted that the reins of power had passed to a new generation.
A doctor contacted by Reuters on Saturday said inflammation of the bladder was a fairly common condition and was usually caused by an infection.
"The idea of the tests may be to make sure there's nothing more serious -- to make sure it is not cancerous," said the doctor, who declined to be identified.
